Meeting header:
Date: 2028-02-20
Time: 16:00 PT / 23:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Alicia Chen (Head of Search - SearchLytics), Ravi Patel (CTO), Ben Ortiz (Sr Data Engineer)

Auto-generated summary: quick demo of hosted embeddings + rerank endpoints for improving search relevance, discuss POC and security.

00:00 Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood Inference, and with me is Maya our solutions engineer. Today we'll walk through how our hosted API can handle embeddings generation plus a separate reranker step to improve search relevance.
00:12 Alicia (SearchLytics): Thanks. We're excited, we've been looking at hybrid approaches, so curious how you guys fit in with our Elastic + vector store setup.
00:20 Jordan: Great. Quick agenda: architecture overview, demo of embeddings endpoint, then reranker walkthrough and example search pipeline, then security/Q&A, and next steps.
00:34 Maya (Redwood SE): I'll kick off with the architecture slide, uh, bear with me while I share. Essentially most customers use Redwood hosted API for embeddings generation and a lightweight reranker on top. So the flow is: ingest docs -> embeddings -> index in vector store -> retrieve candidates -> call Redwood reranker to re-score the top K. That lets you keep lexical results from Elastic and re-rank via semantic scores.
01:05 Ravi (SearchLytics): When you say reranker, is that a separate endpoint? Does it run on the same model as embeddings or a different family?
01:12 Maya: Good question. It's a separate endpoint. Typically customers use a smaller embedding model for vectors and then use a dedicated reranker model that's optimized for pairwise scoring. We expose both as hosted endpoints — embeddings and rerank. You can pick model variants, e.g., our recommended open-model-family: rwd-embed-1 and rwd-rerank-1 (note: model names sometimes auto transcribed differently in notes).
01:40 Ben (SearchLytics): Latency wise, what's the RTT for a rerank call on top 10 candidates?
01:46 Maya: For hosted we usually see 60-150ms per request for a 10-candidate rerank depending on model and request size; with batching and our continuous batching runtime you can push throughput down to 20-40ms per item average for high QPS, but that involves batching tradeoffs. We do have latency SLO tiers if you need guaranteed p50/p90.
02:10 Alicia: We need sub-200ms p95 for search interactions. Is that realistic?
02:16 Maya: Yes, for Top-10 rerank with rwd-rerank-1 on hosted in our lowest-latency config customers see p95 ~150-220ms. If you need consistently lower, Dedicated GPUs with pinned pools are the next step.
02:30 Ravi: Cost is the other side — if we hit peak queries that could be expensive. Do you have suggestions to optimize cost?
02:37 Maya: Absolutely — common levers are: reduce vector dim / use smaller embed model, shard reranker to only top-5, use prefix/KV caching for categorical prefixes, and serve lower-cost model at off-peak times with automated fallback. Redwood Optimize will also give recommendations based on your traffic patterns.
03:02 Jordan: We'll also send a cost estimate for your query profile once you share sample logs. That usually helps decide hosted vs dedicated.
03:15 [Maya screenshare: demo console]
03:20 Maya: Ok I'm calling the embeddings endpoint for a sample doc. Demo note: the console auto shows token counts and estimated cost per call.
03:33 Jordan: We've also integrated streaming responses and function-calling for LLM outputs but for reranker it's a synchronous score response: give two texts (query, doc) or pass batch of doc summaries and get scores back.
04:01 Ben: Is the reranker input format JSON with fields, or do you accept precomputed vectors?
04:06 Maya: Reranker accepts raw text pairs; for vector-based hybrid pipelines you normally compute embedding vectors with embeddings endpoint and store them. Reranker operates on text pairs or you can send the candidate doc snippets. We do support passing embeddings to a rerank variant if you want to avoid re-embedding, but typically text pairs are used because the reranker model was trained on text interactions.
04:35 Alicia: Any limitations with token size? Our doc snippets can get long.
04:40 Maya: We recommend summarizing or truncating to relevant chunks. We also have structured input support where you pass title + snippet fields, the model handles it. For long context we recommend chunking and candidate aggregation.
05:05 Ravi: Let's talk security: we need SOC2, SAML SSO, customer-managed keys and data residency options.
05:14 Jordan: We are SOC2 certified, we support SAML/SSO integrations and RBAC via the Console. For encryption at rest we integrate with KMS of major clouds — you can bring your keys. For Private/Private deployments and VPC peering we have options if you need dedicated network isolation. We'll share the security pack after this call.
05:40 Ben: Do you retain customers' raw docs when using hosted API? Our legal requires limited retention.
05:45 Jordan: By default hosted customers can opt-in to retention policy; we provide configurable retention windows and will not use customer data to train models unless explicit. We'll include retention settings in the security doc.
06:02 [demo continues: console call example, code snippet shown]
06:15 Maya: Here's a quick code example: call embeddings endpoint, upsert vectors to your vector DB (we demo with Elastic + a vector plugin), then on query you retrieve top 50 lexical hits and top 10 vector hits, merge, then send top 10 to Redwood reranker endpoint with JSON array of candidate snippets to get back ranked ids.
06:47 Alicia: That hybrid merge logic is similar to what we run today. Curious if Redwood offers an opinionated middleware or sample repo?
06:55 Maya: Yes we have a reference app and quickstart on GitHub. I'll drop the link in the notes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/search-quickstart (note: placeholder in transcript).
07:10 Ravi: For bulk re-ranking (e.g., nightly batch re-ranks for personalization), do you recommend the same rerank endpoint?
07:18 Maya: For offline batch work you can use larger batch sizes or dedicated Dedicated pool for throughput. Our batching optimizer and async endpoints are better suited for large backfills.
07:30 Ben: What about model drift and evals? We need to monitor relevance metrics over time.
07:36 Jordan: Redwood Optimize ties into your eval sets and can alert on regressions. We recommend a small set of golden queries and quality checks each deploy. We'll help set that up in the POC.
07:55 [transcript continues with demo walkthrough, bench numbers, slight audio interference]
15:12 Maya: ...and here's the benchmark spreadsheet we typically use, it has columns for p50/p95 latency, cost per 1k queries, and throughput. We'll send this after. Link: https://redwood.co/benchmarks/search-bench.xlsx
15:40 Alicia: Can you briefly explain quantization and if it impacts reranker quality?
15:48 Maya: Sure — quantization reduces model precision to speed up inference and reduce memory usage. For many reranker models quantization (4-bit/8-bit) is viable with minimal quality drop but depends on model. We can run quick A/B tests during POC.
16:10 Ravi: Any concerns integrating with our existing Elastic cluster? We run 7.x with a vector plugin.
16:18 Maya: That's pretty common. You can keep your current index, store embeddings in the vector field, and call rerank for final ranking. We also support direct connectors if you want to centralize.
16:35 Ben: What about cold-start performance? If a new doc is indexed and first query happens, do you do anything special?
16:42 Jordan: For cold-start you can pre-warm embeddings during ingest; the runtime caches frequent prefix vectors and we have warm-up APIs for Dedicated capacity.
17:00 [short pause, background noise]
20:05 Alicia: Ok this is helpful. We're leaning to start with hosted to validate relevance improvement then consider Dedicated as traffic ramps.
20:15 Jordan: Sounds good. POC approach: 2-week sandbox, run your 10k sample queries, compare baseline vs our rerank improvement metrics and provide a cost + latency report.
20:30 Ravi: Approvals needed from procurement and security team. We'll loop them in after we see security docs.
20:40 Maya: We'll include a SOC2 summary and KMS integration doc in the pack. Also a short runbook for incident response.
21:05 Ben: One more question on rate limits and quotas — we have spiky traffic. How do you handle bursts?
21:12 Jordan: Hosted has burst capacity options; for predictable bursts we recommend reserved throughput or autoscaling policies in Dedicated. Also auto-fallback to cheaper model variants if quota hits are configured.
22:00 [Maya types, shares example curl commands: embeddings POST, rerank POST]
25:40 Maya: Example rerank response: returns a list of candidate ids with scores in descending order, plus optional explanation tokens if you enable structured output.
26:05 Alicia: That explanation output might help for debugging but not for production.
26:12 Maya: Yeah it's opt-in.
30:00 Jordan: Quick recap: we'll send pricing, security docs, benchmark sheet, and reference app; you share sample dataset and queries; then schedule POC kickoff.
30:20 Alicia: Can you also include suggested success metrics? We'll need to show improvement in MRR and clicks.
30:30 Jordan: We'll propose a short list: MRR improvement, click-through lift for top-3, p95 latency under target, and cost per query delta.
31:00 Ravi: That sounds reasonable. When can we expect the materials?
31:06 Jordan: We'll aim to send everything within 48 hours.
31:12 Ben: Perfect. Any other questions?
31:20 [silence, then quick questions about invoice terms]

35:18 Jordan: Dedicated has monthly and annual reserved options; we'll include that in pricing.

36:15 Alicia: Thanks, talk soon.
